newsitem.title: UK: British utilities hit by budget tax moves.
newsitem.headline: British utilities hit by budget tax moves.

text.p: Shares in British utilities were hit on Wednesday by worries about budget proposals to cut capital allowances on long-life assets -- what traders described as the "backdoor equivalent to a windfall tax".

Shares across the electricity, water and power sectors fell across the board. Notable losers included Anglian Water, down 10-1/2p at 560p, Yorkshire Water, down 5-1/2p at 674p, and Severn Trent, down nine pence at 657-1/2p.
Among energy and power companies, British Gas was down one penny at 228p, Powergen lost seven pence to 570p and National Power was off 4-1/2p at 452p.
Utilities have been hit recently by worries a Labour government could introduce a windfall tax on privatised utilities' profits.
"The windfall tax might have been a one-off and it would have come all in one go. But this is a longer-term affair," one dealer said.

Traders said utilities, with major fixed assets and supply networks were likely to be hard hit by the tax moves. The Financial Times noted that the proposal could "yield as much as Labour's version over the life of a parliament."
